questions.question: How does Owen use irony in the poem to critique the romanticization of war?
questions.solution_html:
• How does Owen use irony to critique the romanticization of war?
  • Ans: Wilfred Owen uses irony to critique the romanticization of war in "The Send-Off".
  • The title suggests farewell to soldiers going to war -- poem's highlights harsh realities of war.
  • -- uses imagery and symbolism to convey irony of war's romanticization (the "flowers" and
  • "bells" typically associated with joy), serve as contrast to the horrors of war.
  • Contrast between expectation and reality: contrast between the expected glory of war and the
  • harsh reality of death, injury, and trauma. This is a powerful irony, critiquing the
  • romanticization of war. -- describes the soldiers' departure as a sombre, eerie event, rather
  • than a celebratory send-off. This irony underscores the reality that war -brutal and devastating
